subject: Gradated response lanes and volume step-down pricing
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@helixai.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on uptime tiers / regional failover discounts

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — HelixAI is excited about Redwood's routing and caching story. Before we move the procurement thread forward, my leadership wants a concise answer to a couple of things about SLA packaging and economics:

1) How do your uptime tiers map to credits if we fail over between US and EU regions? We run a multi-region setup and want to understand credit calculations when traffic shifts during failover windows.

2) For committed monthly spend, what is the step-down discount schedule? Specifically: 1) standard 99.9/99.95/99.99 bands, and 2) a volume cadence where we get larger discounts after 500k / 1M generated tokens per month.

3) If we require a canary fallback to a smaller quantized model during load spikes, is there an SLA carve-out or reduced credit liability?

We have a procurement kickoff Friday; can you send a short pricing spreadsheet and an operations note we can share with finance and infra?

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Ops
HelixAI

--
HelixAI | ops@helixai.com

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@helixai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on uptime tiers / regional failover discounts

Maya — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise spreadsheet (slas_pricing_v3.xlsx) and a short canary playbook excerpt. Below are the high-level answers so you have something to share in your kickoff:

1) Cross-region failover credits: credits are prorated to the impacted request count in the region reporting the SLO miss. If traffic shifts from US to EU during a sustained outage, we calculate credits against the region where the incident originated (on-call region). For multi-region failovers initiated by the customer, we provide a blended-credit approach in the first 24h to avoid double-crediting. Details in tab "CreditsCalc" in the spreadsheet.

2) Volume step-downs: our committed discount bands are volume-tiered and applied to monthly seat/token pricing. Example in the sheet: 0-499k tokens = list, 500k-999k = 8% discount, >=1M = 15% discount. We can offer a stepped ramp for annualized commitments (12 month ramp) that accelerates the banding after month 3. If you want an aggressive commercial, Vanessa can propose a tiered rebate tied to true-up cadence.

3) Canary fallback carve-out: using a smaller quantized model as a graceful degradation path is supported; we treat that as a compatibility fallback. SLA credits apply based on correctness of service (latency/availability) of the *served* variant. However we offer a limited carve-out for planned canaries (pre-declared canary windows) where availability credits are reduced if degrade-to-quantized is part of your runbook. See the "Canary" notes in the attached playbook.

Next steps: I suggest a 30m call with procurement + infra to run the spreadsheet and show the credit calc. Friday looks open at 10:00am PT for me. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slas_pricing_v3.xlsx (pricing matrix), canary-fallback-playbook.pdf (excerpt)

Maya — quick operational clarifications from eng/ops:

• Blended credit treatment is automatic when our routing service detects an induced cross-region failover that meets the incident signature (sustained > 5m of region-level SLO miss with traffic shift >20%). You do not need to open a case to trigger the calculation, but opening an incident helps speed manual reconciliations for edge-cases. We record region tags and tracer spans — examples exported in the playbook excerpt.

• Evidence for audits: we can provide an "evidence bundle" containing tracer IDs, request sampling logs, and the KV cache invalidation timeline for the canary window. Standard bundle turnaround is 5 business days; expedited 2 business days with admin-level access.

• Commercial counter: for a 9-month pilot commit, we can move the larger-band threshold to 800k tokens/month for only the first 3 months of the pilot (a trial accelerator), after which it reverts to the standard 1M band unless you extend. We also propose a modest onboarding credit (1% of first-quarter spend) to help offset migration testing. Vanessa — can you prepare a short SOW addendum for pricing terms and onboarding credit?

If that sounds OK we'll confirm the Friday 10am PT slot and circulate a short agenda (pricing walk, credit calc walkthrough, audit evidence ask).

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Principal, Reliability Engineering (Partnering with Sales Ops)
Redwood Inference
